items.title: The Four Conditions That Give Rise to All Dharmas

items.zh: 又有四緣。一、因緣，二、等無間緣，三、所緣緣，四、增上緣。因緣者，謂種子。
items.en: Further, there are four conditions: first, the causal condition; second, the condition of immediate succession; third, the object-condition; fourth, the dominant condition. The causal condition is the seed.

items.zh: 等無間緣者，謂若此識無間，諸識決定生，此是彼等無間緣。所緣緣者，謂諸心心所所緣境界。
items.en: The condition of immediate succession is this: when this consciousness ceases without interruption, a consciousness of the same kind necessarily arises — this ceasing consciousness is the condition of immediate succession for that arising one. The object-condition is the object taken by mind and its mental factors.

items.zh: 增上緣者，謂除種子，餘所依，如眼及助伴法。望眼識，所餘識亦爾。又善不善性能取愛非愛果。如是等類，名增上緣。
items.en: The dominant condition is, apart from the seed, every other basis it depends on — such as the eye, and its accompanying factors. What holds for eye-consciousness holds equally for the rest. Further, a wholesome or unwholesome nature is capable of securing a desirable or undesirable result. Conditions of this whole kind are called the dominant condition.

items.zh: 又由種子故，建立因緣。由自性故，立等無間緣。由所緣境故，立所緣緣。由所依及助伴等故，立增上緣。
items.en: Further, it is by reason of the seed that the causal condition is established. It is by reason of self-nature that the condition of immediate succession is established. It is by reason of the object taken that the object-condition is established. It is by reason of the basis depended on, and its accompanying factors, that the dominant condition is established.

items.zh: 如經言：諸因諸緣能生識者，彼即此四。因緣一種，亦因亦緣，餘唯是緣。
items.en: As the sutra says: all the various causes and conditions capable of generating consciousness are precisely these four. The causal condition alone is both cause and condition; the remaining three are conditions only.

items.title: How Many Kinds of "Wholesome" Are There? One Through Three

items.zh: 又如經言：善、不善、無記者，彼差別云何？謂諸善法，或立一種。由無罪義故。
items.en: Further, as the sutra says: wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate — what is the distinction among them? As for wholesome dharmas: they may be established as a single kind, in the sense of being blameless.

items.zh: 或立二種。謂生得善及方便善。
items.en: Or they may be established as two kinds: innate goodness, and goodness cultivated through effort.

items.zh: 或立三種。謂自性善、相應善、等起善。
items.en: Or they may be established as three kinds: intrinsic goodness, associated goodness, and goodness that arises together with them.

items.zh: 或立四種。謂順福分善、順解脫分善、順決擇分善、及無漏善。
items.en: Or they may be established as four kinds: goodness conducive to merit, goodness conducive to liberation, goodness conducive to decisive discernment, and uncontaminated goodness.

items.zh: 或立五種。謂施性善、戒性善、修性善、愛果善、離繫果善。
items.en: Or they may be established as five kinds: goodness by nature of giving, goodness by nature of precepts, goodness by nature of cultivation, goodness as a desirable result, and goodness as the result of freedom from bondage.

items.zh: 或立六種。謂善色、受、想、行、識及擇滅。
items.en: Or they may be established as six kinds: wholesome form, feeling, ideation, formations, and consciousness, together with analytical cessation.

items.zh: 或立七種。謂念住所攝善、正勤所攝善、神足所攝善、根所攝善、力所攝善、覺支所攝善、道支所攝善。
items.en: Or they may be established as seven kinds: goodness comprised in the foundations of mindfulness, in right effort, in the bases of supernormal power, in the faculties, in the powers, in the branches of enlightenment, and in the branches of the path.

items.title: Eight Kinds — Wholesome Deeds in Daily Life

items.zh: 或立八種。謂起迎、合掌、問訊、禮敬業所攝善，讚彼妙說、稱揚實德所攝善，供承病者所攝善，敬事師長所攝善，隨善所攝善，勸請所攝善，迴向所攝善，修無量所攝善。
items.en: Or they may be established as eight kinds: the goodness comprised in rising to greet, joining palms, inquiring after another's wellbeing, and paying reverence; the goodness comprised in praising skilful teaching and extolling genuine virtue; the goodness comprised in attending upon the sick; the goodness comprised in honouring one's teachers; the goodness comprised in rejoicing at another's good; the goodness comprised in exhorting others to practise; the goodness comprised in dedicating merit; and the goodness comprised in cultivating the four immeasurables.

items.title: Nine Kinds — The Stages of Overcoming Affliction

items.zh: 或立九種。謂方便、無間、解脫、勝進道所攝善，及軟、中、上、世、出世道所攝善。
items.en: Or they may be established as nine kinds: goodness comprised in the preparatory path, the uninterrupted path, the path of liberation, and the path of further advancement; together with goodness comprised in the weak, middling, and superior paths, and in the mundane and supramundane paths.

items.zh: 或立十種，謂有依善、無依善、聞所生善、思所生善、律儀所攝善、非律儀非不律儀所攝善、根本眷屬所攝善、聲聞乘所攝善、獨覺乘所攝善、大乘所攝善。
items.en: Or they may be established as ten kinds: goodness with a dependency, goodness without a dependency, goodness born of learning, goodness born of reflection, goodness comprised within formal precepts, goodness comprised neither within formal precepts nor their absence, goodness comprised in the fundamental act and its preliminaries, goodness comprised in the Śrāvaka Vehicle, goodness comprised in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, and goodness comprised in the Great Vehicle.

items.zh: 又立十種。謂欲界繫善；初、二、三、四、靜慮繫善；空無邊處、識無邊處、無所有處、非想非非想處繫善；無漏所攝善。
items.en: Further, they may be established as ten kinds: goodness bound to the desire realm; goodness bound to the first, second, third, and fourth meditative absorptions; goodness bound to the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; and uncontaminated goodness.

items.zh: 又有十種。謂十善業道。又有十種。謂無學正見，乃至正解脫、正智。又有十種。謂能感八福生，及轉輪王善，及趣不動善。
items.en: Further, they may be established as ten kinds: namely, the ten wholesome courses of action. Further, they may be established as ten kinds: namely, the adept's right view, and so on, down through right liberation and right knowledge. Further, they may be established as ten kinds: namely, the goodness capable of bringing about the eight kinds of blessed rebirth, the goodness of a wheel-turning king, and the goodness that leads to the unshakable.

items.zh: 如是等類，諸善差別。
items.en: Differences of the wholesome, of this and similar kinds, are to be understood accordingly.

items.title: Two Meanings of "Wholesome," and What Makes Something Unwholesome

items.zh: 略說善有二種義。謂取愛果義，善了知事及彼果義。
items.en: Briefly stated, "wholesome" carries two meanings: the meaning of securing a desirable result, and the meaning of rightly understanding a matter, together with its result.

items.zh: 不善法者，謂與善法相違，及能為障礙，由能取不愛果故，及不正了知事故。
items.en: As for unwholesome dharmas: they are what runs contrary to wholesome dharmas, and what is capable of obstructing them — because they secure an undesirable result, and because they prevent the right understanding of a matter.

items.title: Four Kinds of Neither Wholesome Nor Unwholesome

items.zh: 無記法者，略有四種。謂異熟生，及一分威儀路、工巧處及變化。
items.en: Indeterminate dharmas, briefly stated, are of four kinds: karmic-ripening arising; and a portion of comportment, of craft, and of transformation.

items.zh: 若諸工巧但為戲樂，不為活命，非習業想，非為簡擇，此工巧處業是染污；餘是無記。如工巧處，威儀路亦爾。
items.en: If any craft is pursued purely for amusement, not to sustain one's livelihood, not out of habituated purpose, and not for the sake of discernment, then that act of craft is defiled; the rest is indeterminate. As with craft, so too with comportment.

items.zh: 變化有二種。謂善及無記。
items.en: Transformation is of two kinds: wholesome, and indeterminate.

items.title: The Eye, Counted One Through Six Ways

items.zh: 復次，眼有一種。謂能見色。或立二種。謂長養眼、異熟生眼。
items.en: Further, the eye is of one kind: that which is capable of seeing form. Or it may be established as two kinds: the nourished eye, and the eye arisen from karmic ripening.

items.zh: 或立三種。謂肉眼、天眼、慧眼。或立四種。謂有瞚眼、無瞚眼、恒相續眼、不恒相續眼。恒相續者，謂色界眼。
items.en: Or it may be established as three kinds: the fleshly eye, the divine eye, and the eye of wisdom. Or it may be established as four kinds: the blinking eye, the unblinking eye, the continuously enduring eye, and the not continuously enduring eye. The continuously enduring eye is the eye of the form realm.

items.zh: 或立五種。謂五趣所攝眼。或立六種。謂自相續眼、他相續眼、端嚴眼、醜陋眼、有垢眼、無垢眼、
items.en: Or it may be established as five kinds: the eye comprised within each of the five destinies. Or it may be established as six kinds: the self-continuing eye, the other-continuing eye, the handsome eye, the unsightly eye, the defiled eye, and the undefiled eye.

items.title: The Eye, Counted Seven Through Eleven Ways

items.zh: 或立七種。謂有識眼、無識眼、強眼、弱眼、善識所依眼、不善識所依眼、無記識所依眼。
items.en: Or it may be established as seven kinds: the eye accompanied by consciousness, the eye not accompanied by consciousness, the strong eye, the weak eye, the eye that serves as basis for a wholesome consciousness, the eye that serves as basis for an unwholesome consciousness, and the eye that serves as basis for an indeterminate consciousness.

items.zh: 或立八種。謂依處眼、變化眼、善業異熟生眼、不善業異熟生眼、食所長養眼、睡眠長養眼、梵行長養眼、定所長養眼。
items.en: Or it may be established as eight kinds: the physical-basis eye, the transformation eye, the eye arisen from wholesome karmic ripening, the eye arisen from unwholesome karmic ripening, the eye nourished by food, the eye nourished by sleep, the eye nourished by pure conduct, and the eye nourished by meditative absorption.

items.zh: 或立九種。謂已得眼、未得眼、曾得眼、未曾得眼、得已失眼、應斷眼、不應斷眼、已斷眼、非已斷眼。
items.en: Or it may be established as nine kinds: the already-obtained eye, the not-yet-obtained eye, the previously-obtained eye, the never-before-obtained eye, the obtained-then-lost eye, the eye that should be cut off, the eye that should not be cut off, the already-cut-off eye, and the not-yet-cut-off eye.

items.zh: 或立十種者、無。或立十一種。謂過去眼、未來眼、現在眼、內眼、外眼、麁眼、細眼、劣眼、妙眼、遠眼、近眼、
items.en: As for establishing it as ten kinds — there is none. Or it may be established as eleven kinds: the past eye, the future eye, the present eye, the internal eye, the external eye, the coarse eye, the fine eye, the inferior eye, the excellent eye, the distant eye, and the near eye.

items.zh: 如眼如是，耳等亦爾。

blocks.text: Today's reading has three parts. First the **four conditions**, which we have been using since Day 1, are defined formally. Then the treatise counts "wholesome" in one to ten kinds, and names four kinds of the indeterminate. Finally it begins a long series (continued over the next two days) in which each faculty and object is counted in as many ways as possible. These counting passages can feel dry; read them as exercises in seeing one thing from many angles.
One sentence is untranslated (0292b29): "As with the eye, so with the ear and the rest."

items: **The causal condition** (因緣) "is the seed". Venerable Miào Jìng: the seed is "the power that directly produces every dharma".

**The condition of immediate succession** (等無間緣): when one moment of a consciousness ceases, the next moment of the same consciousness necessarily arises. Venerable Miào Jìng: when a moment of eye-consciousness ceases, the next eye-consciousness must follow, "not that ear-consciousness must arise".
**The object condition** (所緣緣): the object of mind and mental factors.
**The dominant condition** (增上緣): every other support apart from the seed, such as the eye, and also the way wholesome or unwholesome nature secures a desirable or undesirable result.

blocks.text: "The causal condition alone is both cause and condition; the remaining three are conditions only." Only the seed actually produces; the rest make way, provide a focus, or assist.

Venerable Miào Jìng's image for immediate succession is "giving up one's seat": the previous moment must step aside for the next. From this he draws a Yogācāra point we met on Day 2: a mind that arises and ceases has this condition, but a "permanent true mind" could not, so Yogācāra does not accept one.

subs.head: Wholesome, counted one to ten ways

blocks.text: "Wholesome" is one kind in the sense of being blameless. Two kinds: innate goodness (生得善), carried from past-life habit and done gladly without thinking, and goodness cultivated through effort (方便善), learned now from teachers and study. Three kinds: **intrinsic** goodness (the eleven wholesome mental factors, beginning with faith), **associated** goodness (the consciousnesses that accompany them), and goodness **arising together with** them (the actions they produce).

items: giving, precepts, and cultivation, which Venerable Miào Jìng says should be practised in that order, from easiest to hardest;
eight wholesome deeds of daily life, including attending upon the sick (Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha ranked caring for the sick first among fields of merit);

the four paths in overcoming each grade of affliction: preparatory, uninterrupted (which cuts the affliction), liberation (the moment after), and further advancement. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that the weakest path cuts the strongest afflictions, which are coarse and easier to see, while the strongest path is needed for the subtlest;
goodness "with a dependency" (seeking a pleasant rebirth or reputation) and "without a dependency" (dedicated to awakening, like the *Diamond Sūtra*'s giving without abiding).

blocks.text: "Briefly stated, 'wholesome' carries two meanings: securing a desirable result, and rightly understanding a matter together with its result." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first is worldly goodness, the second is world-transcending wisdom. Goodness that only produces pleasant results is still within saṃsāra.

Neither wholesome nor unwholesome are: the karmic ripened result, posture, craft, and transformation. But the treatise adds a sharp qualification: a craft pursued purely for amusement, not for a living, not from habit, and not for understanding, is defiled. Master Cháng Bǎi's point from Day 3 applies: the same activity becomes good or bad according to the mind behind it.

The eye is two kinds (nourished and karmically arisen), three (the **fleshly eye**, the **divine eye**, and the **eye of wisdom**), four, five, six, seven, eight, "ten — there is none", and eleven. Venerable Miào Jìng explains the three eyes: the fleshly and divine eyes are made of refined matter; the wisdom-eye is mental, and here it includes the Dharma-eye. In a Buddha all are called the Buddha-eye.
Notice the honest "there is none". The treatise does not force a category to complete a pattern. That matters for Day 22, when all the counts are added up.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the causal condition among the four?
quiz.why: "The causal condition is the seed." A belongs to the dominant condition, B is the object-condition, D the condition of immediate succession. Venerable Miào Jìng: the seed is "the power that directly produces every dharma" — that is the causal condition; citing the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, he adds that the ālayavijñāna's seeds and the first seven consciousnesses are causal conditions for each other.

quiz.q: What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for the condition of immediate succession, and what Yogācāra position does he draw from it?
options: a relay baton; all dharmas arise at once
waves on water; consciousness and object are one
"giving up one's seat" — the previous moment must cease and make room for the next to arise; hence Yogācāra does not accept a permanent true mind
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "If it doesn't cease, the next moment cannot arise. It has to step aside and give up its seat; only then can the next moment arise." From this he argues that an arising-and-ceasing mind has this condition, while a "permanent true mind" hardly can — the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* does not accept such a mind, the *Awakening of Faith* does. B is exactly what this rules out. He also urges students to note unresolved questions and keep studying rather than hide them.

quiz.q: Citing the sutra, the treatise says the causes and conditions that generate consciousness are just these four. Which of them is "both cause and condition"?
options: only the causal condition; the other three are conditions only
quiz.why: "The causal condition alone is both cause and condition; the remaining three are conditions only." Venerable Miào Jìng: the main force is called "cause," what helps is called "condition"; consciousness needs all four — none can be missing. Master Cháng Bǎi: only the seed genuinely produces its result; faculty, object, and the preceding moment merely supply the circumstances a result needs to appear.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of wholesome, and what is "intrinsic goodness"?
options: intrinsic, associated, and co-arising goodness; intrinsic goodness is the eleven wholesome mental factors beginning with faith
good of body, speech, and mind
quiz.why: "Or they may be established as three kinds: intrinsic goodness, associated goodness, and goodness that arises together with them." Venerable Miào Jìng: intrinsic goodness "is the eleven wholesome mental factors"; associated goodness is the six consciousnesses associated with them — "like someone neither good nor bad who does good when with good people"; co-arising goodness is bodily and verbal action, good both in what initiates it and what it produces. C is the first three of the fivefold scheme.

quiz.q: In overcoming one grade of affliction, what is the order of the four paths the treatise lists?
options: the preparatory path, the uninterrupted path, the path of liberation, the path of further advancement
quiz.why: "Goodness comprised in the preparatory path, the uninterrupted path, the path of liberation, and the path of further advancement." Master Cháng Bǎi: the preparatory path builds towards the breakthrough, the uninterrupted path cuts the affliction, the path of liberation is the moment after, and the path of advancement goes on to what remains. Venerable Miào Jìng notes that this preparatory path comes after the path of seeing, not the four preparatory stages before it. D is the other grouping in the same sentence.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what two meanings does "wholesome" briefly carry?
options: benefit to self and to others
securing a desirable result; and rightly understanding a matter, together with its result
quiz.why: "Briefly stated, 'wholesome' carries two meanings: the meaning of securing a desirable result, and the meaning of rightly understanding a matter, together with its result." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first is worldly goodness, the second world-transcending — so B is an interpretation, not the text's wording. Unwholesome dharmas "run contrary to wholesome dharmas, and … obstruct them," since they secure an undesirable result and prevent right understanding.

quiz.q: When the eye is established as three kinds, what are they?
options: nourished, karmically arisen, and transformation eyes
the fleshly eye, the divine eye, and the eye of wisdom
quiz.why: "Or it may be established as three kinds: the fleshly eye, the divine eye, and the eye of wisdom." A mixes the two kinds (nourished and karmically arisen) with the transformation eye from the eight; B is part of the four; C is part of the eleven. Master Cháng Bǎi: the wisdom-eye is not physical but the mind's capacity to see into things — the root of the expression "an eye for talent."
